test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: The pyruvate is converted into lactic acid which is a three-carbon molecule.
Carbon dioxide is more soluble in water than oxygen.
The walls of the alveoli contain an extensive network of blood-vessels.
The respiratory pigment is present in the white blood corpuscles.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The respiratory pigment is present in the white blood corpuscles.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The respiratory pigment hemoglobin is actually present in the red blood corpuscles (RBCs), not the white blood corpuscles (WBCs).
 
• White blood corpuscles are mainly responsible for immune responses and do not carry respiratory pigments.
 
• RBCs contain hemoglobin which binds to oxygen and facilitates its transport throughout the body.
 
• WBCs include various types of cells such as neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils, which play different roles in the immune system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pyruvate and Lactic Acid**

 
 
• Pyruvate is the end product of glycolysis, a process that breaks down glucose to produce energy.
 
• In anaerobic conditions (lack of oxygen), pyruvate is converted into lactic acid, which is a three-carbon molecule.
 
• This conversion allows glycolysis to continue by regenerating NAD+, which is essential for the glycolytic pathway.
 
 
 
• **Solubility of Gases**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is more soluble in water than oxygen (O₂) due to its higher polarity and ability to react with water to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃).
 
• This increased solubility of CO₂ is important for its transport in the blood and for maintaining acid-base balance in the body.
 
 
 
• **Alveoli and Blood Vessels**
 
 
• The alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs.
 
• The walls of the alveoli are extremely thin and contain an extensive network of capillaries to facilitate the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between the air in the alveoli and the blood.
 
 
 
• **Respiratory Pigment**
 
 
• Hemoglobin is the main respiratory pigment in humans and is present in red blood cells (erythrocytes).
 
• It binds to oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues, facilitating oxygen transport throughout the body.
 
• Hemoglobin also carries a portion of the body's carbon dioxide back to the lungs for exhalation.
